transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, um… I guess I’m here because work’s been getting a little difficult. I’m a cashier, and sometimes at the register I sort of… get stuck doing things that don’t really match what’s happening. Like I’ll tap the scanner in a pattern, or just freeze with my hand over the cash drawer while the customer is standing there waiting.

It’s not like I’m trying to cause a problem or anything. I know it probably sounds strange. But last week I got written up for it, so I thought maybe I should talk to someone. Is that… the kind of thing you can help with?
When you get stuck tapping or freezing, does it happen because you feel you have to do it to relieve a strong inner urge or prevent something bad from happening?

Um… no, I don’t think it’s like that exactly. I’m not doing it because I think something bad will happen if I don’t, at least not that I can explain.

It’s more like I just get caught in it for a moment at the register—like tapping the scanner in some pattern, or my hand just sort of stops over the cash drawer while the customer’s waiting. I know it doesn’t fit what’s going on, and I’m embarrassed by it. It’s been enough that I got written up last week, so… I figured I should ask about it before it becomes a bigger problem.
When those moments happen, do you hear or see things that other people don’t?

Um… I wouldn’t say I see things, not really. But… sometimes I do hear things. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic or anything.

Most days, it’s like a couple people talking just off to the side of me, or from the stockroom. Sometimes it’s my name, or someone saying I rang something up wrong. And then I look, and there’s nobody there… and nobody else seems to have heard it.

Is that the kind of thing you mean?
When you hear those voices, do they feel like real people actually speaking nearby?

Yeah… I mean, in the moment they can feel pretty real, like actual people nearby talking. Usually it sounds like a couple of people just off to the side, or like someone calling my name from the stockroom.

But then when I turn around, there’s nobody there, and no one else seems to have heard it. So I know afterward it probably wasn’t… you know, actually someone. Does that make sense?
Have you found yourself feeling emotionally flat or having much less interest in people or activities than you used to?

A little, yeah… I mean, I still care about my wife and my kids. I don’t want it to sound like I don’t.

But I guess I don’t have the same push I used to. Like my son’s at college, and I’ll think, “I should call him,” and then I just… don’t. Or there’s this kayak group I used to meet up with, and I keep not going. Even my little repair projects around the house, I just kind of leave them sitting there.

And when people ask me what’s wrong, I mostly just shrug. It’s not that I’m trying to be rude—I just can’t find much to say. Is that… the kind of thing you mean?
Do you ever feel like your thoughts are not fully your own, or that someone else can put thoughts into your mind?

Um… no, I don’t think so. Not like someone putting thoughts in my head.

I mean, I get distracted or I second-guess myself sometimes, but my thoughts still feel like… mine, I guess. I haven’t really noticed anything like what you’re describing. Is that okay—like, is that the kind of answer you’re looking for?
Before you tap or freeze, do you feel a buildup inside—like an urge or pressure—that gets relieved when you do it?

I’m not sure it feels like an urge, exactly… not like I’m doing it to get relief.

It’s more like I just get stuck for a second. At the register, I’ll start tapping the scanner in this little pattern, or I’ll freeze with my hand over the cash drawer while the customer is standing there waiting. I know it doesn’t fit what I’m supposed to be doing, and I try to snap out of it.

It’s embarrassing, honestly. I wouldn’t have brought it up except it’s been happening enough that last week I got written up for it. Does that answer what you mean?
When you were a child, did you already tend to have unusual difficulty understanding or connecting with other people?

I don’t think so… not in any big way.

I mean, I was probably a little quiet, maybe more comfortable with a few people than a big group, but I had friends. I went to school, did normal kid stuff. I don’t remember feeling like I couldn’t understand people or connect with them.

Unless you mean something more specific? I’m trying to answer it right.
When the tapping or freezing happens, does it feel involuntary—like it just happens even though you don’t want it to?

Yeah… I think that’s a fair way to put it. I don’t really want to do it, especially not with someone standing there waiting.

It’s like I’m at the register and then I just… get stuck. I’ll tap the scanner in this little pattern, or my hand kind of freezes over the cash drawer, and part of me knows, “Okay, stop, just finish the transaction,” but it doesn’t happen right away.

I know it looks strange, and I’m not trying to make a problem. It’s just been happening enough that I got written up last week, which was… pretty embarrassing. Is that the kind of involuntary you mean?
Do you ever have sudden movements or sounds that come out on their own, like blinking, shrugging, throat-clearing, or grunting?

Not really like blinking or grunting, no… at least I don’t think so.

It’s more the thing I was trying to explain at work, where I sort of get caught doing something that doesn’t fit the moment. Like I’ll tap the scanner in a pattern, or I’ll just freeze with my hand over the cash drawer while the customer is waiting. I know that probably sounds odd. It’s not exactly a sound or a shrug, though.

That’s actually why I came in, because it’s been noticeable enough that I got written up last week. I’m sorry if I’m not answering the way you mean.
Have you had any seizures, head injuries, or other brain or nerve problems?

Not that I know of, no.

I’ve never had anything like a seizure that I’m aware of, and I don’t think I’ve had a serious head injury or anything neurological… at least nothing a doctor told me was a brain or nerve problem.

I mean, if there’s something specific you’re looking for, I can try to think harder, but nothing comes to mind.
Do the tapping or freezing episodes happen more when other people are watching you?

Yeah… I think it’s probably worse when someone’s right there watching, like at the register. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, because it’s not like I’m trying to put on some display or anything.

But when a customer is waiting, that’s when I notice I get stuck doing those things that don’t really fit the moment—tapping the scanner in a little pattern, or freezing with my hand over the cash drawer. And then I’m aware they’re waiting, which makes it more embarrassing, and I think it kind of locks me up more.

That’s what got me written up last week, so… yeah, I guess being watched does seem to make it more noticeable. Is that what you mean?
Do you ever feel that other people are deliberately watching you, talking about you, or trying to harm you when there isn’t clear evidence for it?

I don’t think so… not in the way you’re asking, I mean.

I can get self-conscious, especially when someone’s waiting on me or looking at me at work, but I wouldn’t say I know they’re trying to hurt me or anything like that. And I don’t really have proof that people are talking about me.

I guess sometimes I worry what people think, but that’s probably pretty normal, right?
About how long have you been hearing those voices?

Um… I’d say maybe about three months? Around there.

At first I kind of tried to tell myself it wasn’t really happening, or that I was just tired or stressed, so I’m not sure I marked the exact start. But the voices—and those moments that feel more clearly out of place—have been going on for roughly the last three months, I think.

Does that sound like the kind of timeframe you’re asking for?
Have you started using any drugs, or started or changed any medications, around the time these symptoms began?

Um… no, not that I can think of.

I mean, I don’t use drugs, and I haven’t started anything new like that around when this began. Medications… I don’t think there was any change. At least nothing that stands out to me.

If there’s something specific you mean, I can try to think harder, but I don’t believe there was anything like that.
During the times this happens, do you get confused about where you are or what’s going on around you?

I don’t think I get confused exactly… like, I still know where I am and what I’m doing.

Sometimes I get a little thrown off or distracted, I guess, but not like I don’t recognize the place or don’t understand what’s happening around me. At least, I haven’t noticed that. Does that answer what you mean?
When you get stuck like that, does your body ever stay fixed in the same position even when you try to move?

Um… I don’t know if it’s like I physically can’t move exactly.

But yeah, sometimes I sort of freeze up for a moment. Like at the register, I’ll have my hand over the cash drawer and I just… stay there, even though the customer is waiting and I know I should keep going. Or I get stuck tapping the scanner in this little pattern, which sounds silly, but it’s happened enough that last week I got written up for it.

I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but… yeah, I guess my body does get kind of stuck sometimes. Is that what you mean?
When you freeze or start tapping, can someone else get you moving again just by speaking to you or touching your arm?

Usually, yes… I think if someone says my name or tells me, like, “go ahead,” I can sort of snap back and continue.

I don’t think people usually have to touch my arm, at least not often. It’s more like I realize I’m holding things up and then I get moving again. I’m not trying to do it, it’s just… I’ll be tapping the scanner or kind of frozen over the cash drawer, and then someone speaking to me helps me notice it. Does that make sense?
Have other people told you that your speech is hard to follow, or that you jump from one idea to another in a way that doesn’t make sense?

I don’t think so… not that people have said to me directly.

I mean, sometimes I probably explain things in a roundabout way, especially if I’m nervous, but I haven’t had someone tell me I’m not making sense or that I’m jumping all over the place. If I am doing that now, you can tell me—I’m trying to answer clearly.
During these past few months, have you had a period where you felt unusually depressed most of the day nearly every day?

I don’t think so… not like most of the day nearly every day.

I mean, I have days where I feel down or worn out, sure, but I wouldn’t want to call it unusually depressed if that’s not really accurate. I’ve been trying to keep going with work and things. So… no, I don’t think I’ve had a stretch like that. Is that the kind of thing you mean?

Yeah… I think it’s probably worse when someone’s right there watching, like at the register. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, because it’s not like I’m trying to put on some display or anything.

And then I’m aware they’re waiting, which makes it more embarrassing, and I think it kind of locks me up more.

That’s what got me written up last week, so… yeah, I guess being watched does seem to make it more noticeable. Is that what you mean?

inference.note: Catatonia-like motor freezing/stereotyped tapping that is interruptible by speech, plus ~3 months of auditory hallucinations and negative symptoms, raises schizophrenia with catatonic features (F20.2) and keeps unspecified schizophrenia (F20.9) high. No clear substance/medication trigger or disorientation; organic causes not excluded, so F06.8 remains. Functional neurological disorder (F44.4) remains possible because episodes are worse under observation and interruptible, but psychotic symptoms make it less likely as sole diagnosis.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a roughly 3-month psychotic illness with persistent auditory hallucinations, negative symptoms (reduced motivation, social withdrawal, limited spontaneous speech), and prominent catatonic-like motor behavior (freezing, posturing-like immobility, repetitive purposeless tapping). Symptoms are not better explained by substances, known neurologic illness, confusion/delirium, or a primary mood episode. Among the listed options, catatonic schizophrenia best fits the combination of psychosis plus marked psychomotor disturbance.
